description: Get the rule in force today for one rule type in one jurisdiction, with its citation: source URL, verbatim excerpt and the snapshot Juriset stored. Example: `{"rule_type": "minimum_wage", "jurisdiction": "us-wa"}`. The response is the API's: `data` holds the values (described by the JSON Schema at `schema_url`), `effective_from` and `verified_at` date them, `id` is the version id to record with any decision that relies on it (see resolve_version), and `verification` says which models extracted and checked it and whether a person reviewed it. `verified_at` is when the sources were last re-fetched and found unchanged, not the review date (`verification.reviewed_at`); it is null until a newly fetched source has been re-checked once. Read `data` with its schema: optional fields carry defaults there, e.g. a `minimum_wage` tier or exception without `per_unit` is per hour. Where levels stack (e.g. US federal and state overtime) every level comes back as its own entry in `layers`; Juriset never merges them. Informational only, not legal advice (`disclaimer`).

domain.description: The rule type's domain, e.g. `employment`. Optional: when omitted it is looked up from the rule type.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction slug from list_jurisdictions, e.g. `us-wa` (Washington), `us` (US federal), `ca-ab` (Alberta).

rule_type.description: Rule type slug from list_rule_types, e.g. `minimum_wage`, `overtime`.

name: get_rule
title: Get the current rule
